experiment: Increase KV-cache page chunk size from the documented default of 16 to 64, reverting away from the asset-dependent native speculative drafter that failed with FileNotFound.
hypothesis: Larger KV-cache pages reduce the number of page boundaries the paged-attention kernel iterates over per prefill and decode step for the benchmark's short, sequential, greedy sequences, which may lower both TTFT and per-token decode overhead without altering the sampled tokens.
notes: One documented CMD flag changed (--page-chunk-size, --help default 16). No new weights, downloads, credentials, or egress. Preserves /llmd/llmd ENTRYPOINT, --io-impl=zio, --max-context-len=128000, port 8000, and --model=/models/model appended by the runner; all other Dockerfile bytes and ENV lines unchanged, no RUN steps. Page-chunk-size governs KV-cache layout, not sampling, so greedy determinism, golden-output match, finish_reason, streamed-chunk count vs completion_tokens, and all six correctness gates should be unaffected. No measured speedup is claimed; root will build and measure on available GPUs.
risk: If the auto-selected attention backend path does not expose page-chunk-size to its kernel (e.g., a CPU fallback), the change may be inert and fail the 3% keep bar. Larger pages waste a few cache slots on short sequences, and a different page granularity could in principle perturb floating-point rounding enough to flip a borderline greedy token, though the benchmark's clear-top-k golden answers make this unlikely.
